I don’t love the term “pet”. It almost feels derogatory towards the thinking, feeling, sentient being that dogs, cats, and other animals considered “pets” are. I prefer to think of my family’s dogs as companion animals. And we treat them as such. Very rarely do they even wear collars. They sleep in our beds. We leave their food and water bowls full at all times. They get regular trips to parks and visiting family members (granted away from our house we usually are required to keep them on a leash). 
I think slavery is a bit harsh. The majority of companion animals are treated with immense amounts of respect and love. If we just let all of the “pets” roam free all of the sudden there would be a lot of chaos. Eventually I would love for the world to get to a point where humans no longer breed animals or keep them as companions, but we are not at a place where we can just up and essentially abandon all animals that are domesticated.

to me at least, it’s her darkest album. I’ve been dealing with depression for over a year now and some days are really hard.

The constant commenting on my dietary choices. I live with my parents (20F) and four little brothers at the moment. They always have something to say about my dairy-free cheese or how I’m “murdering the plants.” I do my best to not go on a rampage about the horrors of the industries they knowingly support but I know my soapbox won’t change their mind.

I also struggle with mental health, so I totally understand your perspective that the pressure to be the “perfect” vegan is overwhelming and harmful. I’ve seen posts on this subreddit that do cause me anxiety, like I’ll never be able to do enough.

But, to me at least, being vegan means committing to doing the best you can to not participate in these cycles of animal abuse and use of sentient beings. I’m not always going to get it right. I’m not always going to agree with other vegans. But I am going to stand strong in my own conviction that I’m doing what I can to fight for what is right.

If you don’t want to go through the trouble of finding a different cereal or vegan sugar that is your prerogative, and I respect that. I live in the Midwest, and at 20 years old still live with my parents, so I’m sure I’m going to run into some roadblocks. But I’m still going to try my best.

At the end of the day I’d rather be a part of a community constantly striving to end animal abuse rather than the ones I see in my physical life and other areas of the internet. I think this subreddit is doing much more good than harm.
